card.name: Dose amount just before frequency
card.fires_on: The last word of a dose amount or count (times, mg, insert, inhalation, closing parenthesis) right before a frequency like daily, a day, or twice daily in dosing instructions. It also fires on the word time in the idiom 'from time to time'.

modes.label: Dose unit before frequency
modes.description: Word like times, mg, insert or inhalation ending a dose amount, with a daily-frequency phrase expected next.
modes.example: Instill one drop of OXERVATE in the affected eye(s), 6<< times>> a day at 2-hour intervals for

modes.label: Closing bracket after eye(s)
modes.description: The closing parenthesis after eye(s) in a dose line, followed by how often to give it.
modes.example: in the affected eye(s<<)>> three times daily.

modes.label: From time to time
modes.description: The word time in the everyday phrase about something happening occasionally.
modes.example: The fever that Romans developed from time to<< time>>, though, kept their cancer rates well

card.writes: It suppresses 'every year/month/day/week' words, so it steers away from per-period frequency words after a dose amount.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a dosing line where the amount has just ended and a how-often phrase like 'daily' is about to come.
